properties.description:

across northeast Georgia. Given the dry vegetation and low fine
fuel moisture, outdoor fires will be able to spread quickly once
started, increasing the danger of wildfires.

Please refer to your local burn permitting authority on whether
you can burn today. If you do burn, use extreme caution since
fires can quickly get out of hand under these conditions.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 21 at 9:51PM PDT until October 21 at 10:15PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
At 951 PM PDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles southeast of
Valley Of Fire, or 9 miles south of Overton, moving north at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Overton, Echo Bay Campground, Echo Bay, Valley Of Fire and Overton
Beach.

This includes Interstate 15 in Nevada between mile markers 75 and 76.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

If on or near Lake Mead, get away from the water and move indoors or
inside a vehicle. Remember, lightning can strike out to 15 miles from
the parent thunderstorm. If you can hear thunder, you are close
enough to be struck by lightning. Move to safe shelter now! Do not be
caught on the water in a thunderstorm.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Rock slides and mudslides are possible.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wrightwood, Glendora, San Dimas, Pomona, La Verne, Valyermo,
Falling Springs, Angeles Crest Highway between Mount Waterman and
Wrightwood, Angeles Crest Highway between Mount Wilson and Mount

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:49PM MST until October 22 at 2:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Moenkopi Wash in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 200 AM MST /300 AM MDT/.

* At 949 PM MST /1049 PM MDT/, Moenkopi Wash remained above major
flood stage, with only a gradual decrease over the last hour. With
additional heavy rain expected in the Moenkopi Wash basin, flooding
is expected to continue. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Moenkopi Wash.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 8:45pm MST /9:45pm MDT/ the stage was 33.54 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash, Little Colorado River, Moenkopi
Wash and Fivemile Wash.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 2:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 2:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 21 at 9:17PM PDT until October 23 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and seas
7 to 12 feet expected.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Pt. St. George to Cape Mendocino
CA out 10 nm.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Thursday to 9 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
properties.instruction:

vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Cape Mendocino to Pt. Arena CA from 10 to 60 nm
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 21 at 9:17PM PDT until October 22 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, north winds 25 to 30 kt with
gusts up to 40 kt and seas 10 to 14 feet expected. For the
Small Craft Advisory, north winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to
30 kt and seas 7 to 9 feet expected.

* WHERE...Waters from Cape Mendocino to Pt. Arena CA from 10 to
60 nm.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, from 9 PM Thursday to 9 PM PDT
Friday. For the Small Craft Advisory, from 9 AM to 9 PM PDT
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Santa Barbara, CA
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:11PM PDT until October 22 at 2:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
FFWLOX

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Santa Barbara County in southwestern California...

* Until 200 AM PDT.

* At 911 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is
0.7 to 1 inch in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Rock slides and mud slides are likely.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. Rock slides and
mud slides.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas. Rock slides and mud slides.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Portions of southern Santa Barbara County, including the Santa Ynez
Range and the South Coast, and the City of Santa Barbara.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Water can rise rapidly in hilly terrain and in urban areas.

Rock slides and mud slides are likely, especially around mountain and
foothill roadways.

properties.areaDesc: Boise Mountains
properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued October 21 at 10:09PM MDT until October 23 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Crooked burn scar and Wapiti burn scar. Total
rainfall up to 1 inch is possible on the burn scars.

* WHERE...Wapiti and Crooked burn scars in southwest Idaho.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Crooked and Wapiti burn scar is
expected up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near
the Crooked and Wapiti burn scar should prepare for potential
debris flow. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding or debris
flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Crooked and Wapiti burn scar, which may lead to
flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Grandjean and Barber Flat Guard Station.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
